title: 29yo M Severe Falciparum Malaria
background: Migrant forestry worker, arrived from the Thai-Myanmar border in Tak province eleven days ago and now working on a rubber plantation. Six days of intermittent high fever with rigors, initially treated at a pharmacy with paracetamol and an unidentified tablet. He became confused this morning and had one generalised seizure in the truck. He speaks limited Thai and a co-worker is interpreting. He has no health insurance and is worried about the bill.

exam.finding: Cachectic, hot to touch, drowsy and confused, deep acidotic breathing, unable to follow commands in any language
Scleral icterus, pale conjunctivae, dry mucous membranes, no neck stiffness, no rash, retinal whitening and a single retinal haemorrhage on fundoscopy
Sinus tachycardia, bounding then thready pulse, capillary refill 4 seconds, soft systolic flow murmur from anaemia
Deep sighing Kussmaul respirations at 32/min, bibasal fine crackles suggesting early acute lung injury, no consolidation
Tender splenomegaly 4 cm below the costal margin, hepatomegaly 2 cm, no ascites. Handle the spleen gently, splenic rupture is a recognised complication
Jaundiced, hot dry skin, reduced turgor, no petechiae or purpura, no eschar found after a full search including axillae and groin
GCS 9 (E2V2M5), post-ictal, no focal deficit, no meningism, pupils equal and reactive, plantars downgoing. Cerebral malaria is a diagnosis of exclusion after hypoglycaemia is corrected

investigations.name: Thick and thin blood smear
investigations.report: Parasitaemia above 10% is a severe malaria criterion on its own. Circulating schizonts indicate a heavy sequestered load. Repeat the smear 12 hourly to track clearance.

investigations.name: Rapid diagnostic test (HRP2)
investigations.report: Positive. Stays positive for weeks after treatment, so it confirms diagnosis but cannot be used to monitor response.

investigations.name: Capillary glucose
investigations.report: Profound hypoglycaemia. This is a severe malaria criterion, a cause of the seizure and the coma, and it is reversible in 90 seconds. Check it before you attribute anything to cerebral malaria.

investigations.name: Haemoglobin and platelets
investigations.report: Severe anaemia (a severity criterion below 7 g/dL) with thrombocytopenia from haemolysis and sequestration.

investigations.name: Lactate and bicarbonate
investigations.report: Metabolic acidosis with hyperlactataemia. Acidosis is the strongest single predictor of death in severe malaria.

investigations.name: Creatinine and bilirubin
investigations.report: Acute kidney injury and jaundice, two further severity criteria. This patient meets at least six.

investigations.name: Blood cultures
investigations.report: Sent before antibiotics. Concomitant Gram negative bacteraemia occurs in up to 10% of severe malaria and is easily missed.

data.label: Glucose first in any febrile patient with reduced consciousness

doseMap.IV dextrose bolus: 50 mL of 50% dextrose IV, then 10% dextrose infusion. Recheck glucose every hour, hypoglycaemia recurs, especially on quinine

data.label: Partial neurological improvement
data.narrative: GCS improves from 9 to 12 within ten minutes of the dextrose. The residual impairment is real cerebral malaria, but you now know how much of it was reversible sugar.

data.label: Thick and thin smear plus rapid diagnostic test, without delaying treatment
IV artesunate, the only correct first line drug for severe malaria

doseMap.Artesunate IV: 2.4 mg/kg IV at 0, 12 and 24 hours, then daily. Artesunate reduces mortality by about a third compared with quinine. Do not give oral therapy to a patient who cannot swallow, and do not wait for the smear if the suspicion is high

doseMap.Broad spectrum IV antibiotics: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV daily, until blood cultures exclude coexisting bacteraemia
doseMap.Cautious crystalloid resuscitation: Small aliquots with reassessment. Aggressive fluid loading increases pulmonary oedema and mortality in severe malaria

data.label: Find a proper interpreter and treat first, sort the billing later (Empathy)
data.narrative: The co-worker interpreting is frightened and is softening everything you say. You find a Burmese speaking cleaner who has worked here nine years and ask her to interpret properly, so that consent for transfusion is real rather than a nod. You also tell the co-worker to stop worrying about the bill tonight, because emergency care for a non-insured migrant is covered by a fund most people do not know exists, and because a man with 14% parasitaemia should not be making financial decisions.

data.label: Transfuse, monitor and admit to ICU

doseMap.Packed red cell transfusion: For haemoglobin below 7 g/dL with severe malaria. Transfuse slowly with attention to fluid overload

data.label: Clinical improvement
data.narrative: Parasitaemia falls to 4% at 24 hours and 0.2% at 48 hours. GCS 15 by day 3. Acidosis resolves without dialysis. Watch for post-artesunate delayed haemolysis at 7 to 21 days, which will bring him back if nobody warns him.

data.label: Disposition
data.narrative: Full oral artemisinin combination course completed. Discharged day 7 with written return advice in Burmese for delayed haemolysis, and the plantation is notified so the other twelve workers can be screened. Two of them are positive and asymptomatic.
